Contract:
SDD v2 has exactly two mandatory semantic approval boundaries.
1. **Spec approval.** The complete intended spec set exists as actual files, passes structural checks, and receives one fresh independent semantic review of the current artifacts. The author resolves findings. Any semantic edit invalidates the old review and requires one fresh review of the changed set. The operator then approves the specs themselves and the canonical specs record `ARTIFACT_APPROVAL_MARKER` approval #1. 2. **Ticket approval.** Actual tickets and indexes exist, each ticket passes the mechanical authoring check, and one fresh independent reviewer checks the complete actual ticket set against the approved specs. The operator then approves task decomposition and the test plan in one decision. The owning task index records `ARTIFACT_APPROVAL_MARKER` approval #2. Any semantic ticket or index edit invalidates the old review and approval.
Reviewers are bounded calls, not durable sessions. They never edit targets and do not exchange JSON state with the orchestrator. The author may reason about its own draft before dispatch, but self-review never substitutes for the independent review at either boundary.
Resume state is always reconstructible from human-readable approval markers, specs, tickets, Execution Log, Git, and current tool output. Mechanical checks validate marker shape and membership; the model uses Git evidence to judge semantic staleness. No `.sdd-session.md`, plan digest, critic journal, content hash, or worker checkpoint is part of correctness.
